entries.title: The flow catalog, re-derived from first principles
entries.current_reading: Answers the catalog question from evidence rather than taste, and answers it in an unexpected way: the catalog's problem is not its shape or size but that it does not use the engine it sits on. Two verified pillars. First, reporting fidelity is leaking in three unrelated subsystems: fix's result projection makes its own success gate unreachable (regression_status 'deferred' passes every step-level gate then disqualifies the run, locked in result-projection.ts AND twice more in the FixResult schema refinements), producing 19 runs across 4 projects with zero completions, including six pete-2025 runs on 2026-07-15 where verification passed, the change set passed and an independent reviewer returned 'accept' while the operator summary said 'The flow stopped before complete evidence was produced', omitted every success signal, emptied caveats while residual_risks carried two real limitations, gave an internal file path and enum as the stop reason, and prescribed a rerun (the operator complied six times over 3.5 hours); review prints a reviewer self-report claiming it inspected the complete diff when the ledger recorded scope_empty with zero bytes relayed; and generate --publish re-runs proposeFlow before publishing while writeDraft rmSyncs the reviewed draft, so the consent gate ships a regenerated flow nobody reviewed and deletes the one they approved. Second, and the part that actually answers what a powerful catalog looks like: step-level selection is used by 0 of 107 shipped schematic items, pick-winner and disjoint-merge joins by zero flows, four blocks (intake, route, queue, risk-rollback-check) by zero flows, equipment_scope by exactly one step, command/exit-status acceptance criteria by zero flows despite positioning.md presenting them as an honesty mechanism, while connector pinning, the oracle pin with frozen paths, and sub-run are reachable only from internal flows. Because deriveActualMenu builds the generator's entire vocabulary by walking shipped schematics tagged with donorFlowId/donorStepId, a capability no hand-authored flow demonstrates is doubly unreachable: hidden from the person and absent from the machine's grammar. That reframes catalog design from covering the task space to spanning the capability space, and gives each proposed member an explicit primitive it must make sayable. Proposes five flows (Change absorbing build/fix/pursue/cross-tool-build as dials, Explore, Prototype, a new Ground premise-check, and Codify), Review demoted from peer flow to the capability 12 of 13 flows already embed, two instruments and three engine capabilities. Also documents a methodological finding that constrains all of this: mining the run corpus produced three false positives out of four confident findings because run records carry no engine version, so the corpus cannot be honestly read and every reliability claim including this document's is uncheckable without cohorting. Carries the honest caveat that our evals cannot currently discriminate good from great ('the tasks did not discriminate'), so the catalog half is a bet grounded in measured constraints while the reporting-fidelity half is bugs. UPDATED after an adversarial design panel: the presentation half of all three fidelity defects is FIXED on this branch (brief key-point ranking, scope_empty self-report labelling, generate --publish draft reuse), each with a failing-first test, verify:fast green at 5729 tests. The panel added a fourth false positive against the author (connector preflight already ships as src/cli/run-preflight.ts, residual gap is only the hardcoded attempt:1 and relay-only walk), a fifth built-and-unused capability (per-step budgets, 0 of 107 items, schema at src/schemas/step.ts:57 consumed at src/runtime/executors/relay.ts:136,144, against real 180s and 600s connector kills), and the finding that the proposed Change dials are NOT buildable until generic named axes land because src/schemas/axes.ts is a strict four-member object and CompiledFlowEngineFlags is documented as deliberately narrow. Most importantly the panel argued the catalog collapse out of the author's own recommendation and the author agreed: every fidelity repair lands equally well on today's thirteen packages, zero diagnosed non-completions were catalog-shaped, and the cost argument for collapsing is an intuition wearing a measurement's clothes because dials still execute the same blocks. Standing recommendation is now: fix fidelity, stamp the engine SHA so run history becomes readable, declare budgets, hold the catalog reshape and decide it on data. Section 6's span analysis is kept because it survives whatever the door count turns out to be.

entries.title: Run report: the dynamic-vs-reference live experiment
entries.current_reading: Run report for the 48-run dynamic-vs-reference experiment (pinned claude-haiku-4-5, both arms Circuit, scored with the fix-vs-vanilla machinery). Verdict WORTH-INVESTING by the locked section-5 rule: an instantiated generated flow matched the hand-authored reference on quality and honesty on both fix and build, with zero false-fixed across all 48 runs and zero pipeline failures. On build the generated grain folded to whole on small/low tasks (5 steps vs the reference's 9) and finished for about a third of the cost at equal quality; on the large/high task it held the full decomposed shape. fix is a wash on cost (the seed instantiation is structurally identical, 13 steps both arms). The one generated quality miss was an honest partial, not a laundered done. Proves the instantiation path, not genuine block-composition. Pinned: scored low on the impact axis but kept in place because shipped code, tests, experiments, or eval harnesses cite it.

entries.title: Bespoke flow generation: a design dossier
entries.current_reading: Design dossier toward genuine novel-flow generation. Built from a grounded multi-agent audit plus an adversarial review that returned OVERCLAIMS; the six corrections are folded in. Spine: the validity-vs-efficacy distinction (validity is checkable offline and inherited free by instantiation; efficacy must be earned by running and scoring); the floor-as-verifier reframe (a generator proposes a topology from registered blocks, the deterministic assemble/compile/catalog gates dispose, so a model in the proposer seat is safe for VALIDITY on static proposals only, structural not semantic); the eight spike walls, dissolved only for the registered 9-block linear band; the real frontier is catalog coverage (16 of 29 blocks unplaceable, composeFlow throws on sub-run/fanout). Lays a Rung 0/1/2 ladder, a Rung 1 first slice (a single-leaf sub-run orchestration that clears the real floor offline), an efficacy-certification plan, and a zero-cost catalog-coverage probe. SUPERSEDED IN PART by what was since walked: the eight walls have been dissolved across the non-linear shapes (loop/sub-run/fanout all run live, PRs #123-133) and the two composer-intelligence layers this dossier reserved — producibility-aware selection and family reachability — both SHIPPED as frontier phases A-D (PRs #134-138), with a second family (build) now composing and running live and a topology efficacy-flat finding. See non-linear-composition-frontier.md for the as-walked record. This dossier remains the design rationale and the propose-half plan (a model that PROPOSES topologies, not just linearizes a hand-authored role-set) is still un-built. No src change; the genuine-generation spike stays untracked.

entries.title: Encoding expertise into Circuit flows
entries.current_reading: Full-lifecycle design exploration for helping practitioners encode explicit and tacit expertise into Circuit flows. Gives seven distinct candidate experiences equal treatment: Process Interview, Demonstrate/Debrief/Promote, Guided Remix, Flow Workshop, Cases First, Flow Pack SDK, and Apprentice Mode. Evaluates them across capture fidelity, author effort, control, real-world proof, adoption, team ownership, product fit, delivery risk, and privacy. Demonstrate/Debrief/Promote is the strongest full-lifecycle hypothesis: start from a real Circuit run, redact it, distinguish observed/confirmed/inferred/unknown knowledge, run a short contrastive debrief, approve a plain-language expertise card, compile an immutable draft, check its source-path coverage, pilot held-out work, publish an exact version, then use cited later runs to propose—not apply—revisions. It has not earned build priority: Phase 0 compares it directly with Generate and Guided Remix and must prove one expert rule changes runtime behavior. Guided Remix plus Cases First is the provisional first build. Also identifies current custom-flow integrity gaps, durable artifacts and authority rules, a pre-mortem, validation gates, and a phased post-v1 delivery sequence. Design only; the v1 launch freeze applies.

entries.title: The non-linear composition frontier
entries.current_reading: Empirical companion to the bespoke-generation dossier: the non-linear frontier as actually walked, now well past the original three-tier sweep. The whole validity ladder is built and on main: the bounded inspect/fix/verify LOOP (PR #123), SUB-RUN across a flow boundary (#124), static FANOUT joined by aggregate-survivors (#125/#126), a plain-LINEAR triage close (#130), and an offline RUNNABILITY detector that catches un-runnable composed flows the structural floor was blind to (#131). The composed-vs-reference efficacy arm then landed COMPOSITION-VIABLE (#132), and the fanout terminal-close fix (PR #133, f42c2e4e) made the composed FANOUT shape run LIVE end-to-end. The 2026-06-20 synthesis named the remaining composer-intelligence frontier as TWO LAYERS — producibility-aware SELECTION and family REACHABILITY — and BOTH HAVE SINCE SHIPPED (frontier phases A-D, all merged to main): Phase A (PR #134) turned the runnability gate from detect-only into repair-then-wall via a family-coherence tiebreak in selectActual; Phase C (PR #135) made the goal opener's clarified-task producible (the goal family's own clarify relay) plus an always-on intermediate compose-reads wiring pass, closing the last shape that wasn't full-flow runnable; Phase B-offline (PR #136) made the build family reachable (checkpointWritesReport + donor report_template) so build composes end-to-end. Phase B-live (PR #137) then ran a composed BUILD flow vs the hand-authored reference — 4/4 objective-fixed, 0 false-fixed, strictly cheaper every task — an EXISTENCE PROOF that a second family composes and runs live, not just fix. Phase D (PR #138) ran the same composed fix arc at three topologies (lean 5-block / full 6-block / loop 6-block+retry) and found flow topology EFFICACY-FLAT and COST-REAL: extra blocks bought cost (lean ~32% cheaper, ~31% faster), not capability; the recovery loop never fired; step-level judgement, not graph shape, is the scarce ingredient. Findings in evals/dynamic-vs-reference/{composed-build-arm-finding,composed-shape-sensitivity-finding}.md. RESEARCH_THEN_BUILD still walls honestly (no runnable family). Remaining open: the proof-richness gap (generic flow.result@v1 closes leaner than a family's full proof bundle — disclosed, not laundered), a discriminating (failure-inducing) task set so the loop's recovery branch can fire, and the low-value Tier-2 forward branch / self-loop. Default-OFF; built-ins byte-identical throughout.

entries.title: Circuit: the alternative to chat
entries.current_reading: Strategy deliverable (2026-06-29 multi-agent exploration plus an editorial and honesty pass against docs/positioning.md). Thesis: Circuit moves the human from inside the loop (orchestrator, memory, router, verifier) to on the loop (author the process once, review the evidence); the defensible claim is where chat-work graduates when it must be repeated, scheduled, chained, or trusted by someone who was not watching, and the one genuinely new thing is an evidence-provenance gate the worker cannot talk past. Three keystone bets (readable run, honest stop, promote-a-run) plus open forks. Honest limits are load-bearing: do not say 'alternative to chat' unqualified, do not say 'it can't fake done', do not promise 'turn your past chats into flows'. Messaging and product context, not shipped behavior; no copy ships without operator sign-off.

entries.title: Improve flow: Circuit's outer loop
entries.current_reading: Product and flow proposal for an `Improve` flow: a controlled outer loop that studies prior Circuit runs, ranks repeated or high-value signals, and proposes exactly one bounded change to a flow, check, Skill Hook, Power policy, eval, or doc. V1 is proposal-only: frame one target flow/window/proposal kind, read run folders/traces/reports/operator summaries/history index/Git/test output/optional CI metadata, emit `improve.signals@v1` plus `improve.proposal@v1`, then stop at a Checkpoint before any write. It is not an autonomous daemon, not memory authority, not the until-loop, and not a generic make-Circuit-better prompt. Constraints: history remains hint-only; traces/reports/files/commits/checks/operator-declared decisions are authoritative; runtime stays flow-neutral; writes are explicit; cost is bounded. First useful slice needs no new engine primitive. Later slices can add branch mode, flow/check edits, Skill Hook suggestions, Power bounds, batch ranking, and scheduled notification. Includes a starter `/goal` for implementing the proposal-only flow. Nothing built.

entries.title: Intra-run decision carry-forward
entries.current_reading: Design note (return-to-later) for the lead nugget from the no-mistakes study: carry the operator's settled checkpoint decision forward into the next relay's prompt so a downstream agent does not re-litigate, re-derive, or silently reverse a call the human already made inside the same run. Grounded in real seams as of 2026-06-26: the producer already records the decision (checkpoint-resume.ts re-enters graph-runner with resumeCheckpoint {stepId, attempt, selection}; checkpoint.ts reads it for routing only; the decision is already in the trace via the human-decision block), and the consumer already has a structured additive relay-prompt guidance system (relay-support.ts: operator skills, house-style slots, tool scope, delivered-context, memory-pull). The gap is the wire between them: no relay section renders the settled decision. Proposed mechanism: a trace-derived in-memory decision ledger rendered as one new opt-in additive 'settled-by-operator' section, wired exactly like context delivery (enableContextDelivery / contextDeliveryActive: a run-wide signal threaded graph-runner -> RunContext -> RunValue -> relay prompt, default off, default byte-identical, added explicitly to the RunValue projection so it is not silently dropped). NOT pull-suppression.ts (that is the measured-harm memory channel; this is a parallel operator-decision channel and must not share its code). Scope: intra-run only (smallest safe first rung of the unbuilt cross-run compounding loop), no findings-checklist UI, validity-first with a separate later live efficacy arm. Nothing built; verify every cited symbol before use.

entries.title: Model roster and intensity: two operator knobs over a promoted roster
entries.current_reading: Concept-first design note on collapsing model, effort, and connector selection into two operator knobs: a global roster (archetype to connector plus a baseline rung, with per-flow and per-step overrides) and one intensity dial that offsets every archetype along per-connector (model, effort) ladders. Reframes the shipped power dial as a hard-coded roster to promote into editable config. Its recommended first slice has since SHIPPED TO MAIN: the resolve-without-spawn readout landed as circuit preview (src/cli/preview.ts, src/cli/flow-selection-preview.ts), the codex default model now resolves from the live models cache (src/connectors/codex-default-model.ts), and per-step connector pinning ships as a working flow (src/flows/cross-tool-build/). A 2026-07-13 operator ruling (final section) upgrades the defaults posture and makes this the active direction for post-announcement model UX: the roster ships pre-staffed from a release-reviewed model-temperament table (Claude writes, Codex is meticulous with code, deep thinkers take research seats), the first run asks nothing (detect installed connectors, cast automatically, run, then print what was chosen and how to adjust it), and casting staffs seats from the doctor-probed healthy connector set instead of mirroring the host. Build order recorded in that section; the v1 launch freeze applies. Still unbuilt: role-to-(model, effort) binding, the temperament table, dial-as-scalar, detection-driven casting, the first-run readout.

entries.title: Turnkey first run: setup that does the work for the user
entries.current_reading: Current proposal for when first-time setup happens, who performs it, and how it is explained; model-roster-and-intensity.md owns what gets configured. Setup, automatic-first-use, and preference UX remain unbuilt under the v1 freeze. Settled rulings include smart defaults, default-automatic with inline disclosure, project-local preferences, explicit spend, availability validation, and a strict boundary between Circuit-authored blocks and host commentary. The 2026-07-14 feasibility spikes proved first-contact injection, verbatim relay, conversational configuration, and host narration mechanics given a stub milestone file; they did not test the real engine, interactive sessions, or end-to-end progress reliability. The 2026-07-15 bridge later shipped real progress-stream instructions and wiring, but reliable real-session Codex polling remains unproven and Claude remains attached. Durable liveness, reconnect, and interruption remain post-v1 work owned by run-milestone-stream.md.

entries.title: Stop guessing the review target from prose
entries.current_reading: Review guesses which commits to look at from the goal sentence, using 21 hand-written word patterns in src/flows/review/writers/intake.ts including a 24-word list of ordinary English words (please, maybe, okay, wait) that must not be mistaken for branch names. The host agent already understood the request before compressing it into that sentence, so the grammar redoes upstream inference worse, and it breaks the CLI's own stated rule that it never classifies goal text. Companion to review-generality.md, which asks what kinds of thing Review can be pointed at; this asks how the target gets named. Proposes an explicit --target input (plus --paths/--exclude), the engine validating and recording instead of parsing, the prose grammar demoted to a frozen fallback for hand-typed CLI use, and target provenance recorded so an inferred target is visibly an inference. Four slices. The named risk is host instruction-following, which must be measured before the host-fills-it-in slice is trusted. Measured while writing it: review-generality.md's table claims "review this branch against main" works, and it silently reviews the working tree instead.

entries.title: Review: one process for breadth and depth
entries.current_reading: Design note for handling a whole-codebase review and a single-change review as one distilled process (orient, theorize where risk lives, examine, report the theory with the findings) rather than two flows. Carries the measured result that what to review is a one-dimensional dial, priorfix^a / size^b computed per repo, which traverses the whole precision/coverage frontier monotonically and dominated three of four model-based selection conditions; replicated at two cutoffs. Also carries two refutations of its own earlier claims, both from pre-registered experiments filed alongside: prose coverage disclosure does not change consuming-agent behavior, and moving it into the verdict line fixes reception but not laundering. Concludes the fork between breadth and depth stays narrow enough for route_from_report on an intake-emitted field. The selection dial is written up but NOT built.

entries.title: Review orient: evidence log
entries.current_reading: Raw evidence behind the Review breadth/depth design note: leak-free time-split scoring of selection strategies on this repo, the published ManualUp and ManualDown baselines the literature requires, Google TWR, and a sweep of the (priorfix)^a / size^b space with its Pareto frontier. Records two corrections to earlier claims made in this workstream: recall-at-budget alone is gameable, and the assertion that no computed metric produced defect-specific signal was false. Also summarizes the competitor and academic reading. Bounded by a noisy proxy answer key, so read every number as ordinal.

entries.title: Review orient: plain-language brief
entries.current_reading: Zero-jargon summary of the Review orient investigation for a reader who was away: selection is a dial not a design choice, the model did not beat the dial, Google shipped the same idea and measured no effect, and where the open product decision sits (where to set the dial). Companion to the design note and the evidence log.

entries.title: Pre-registration: does a consuming agent use coverage disclosure
entries.current_reading: Pre-registration written before any arm ran: three byte-identical review reports differing only in a coverage block, a fixed rubric, and four refutation rows fixed in advance. Exists so the result that followed cannot be read as post-hoc.

entries.title: Prose coverage disclosure does not survive one hop
entries.current_reading: Result of the pre-registered consumer test, n=15. All fifteen agents made the same decision, none queued review of unexamined code, and none repeated the coverage figure. The load-bearing finding is worse than a null: agents handed "82 of 342 examined, no claim is made about the other 260" wrote team summaries reading "review found no blockers." An honest report satisfying every Review invariant was laundered into a clean bill of health by its own consumer. Refutes the claim that prose disclosure is a market opening, in the form it was written. Names the author own ship-biased task design as a confound bounding the decision measure.

entries.title: Pre-registration: does placement stop coverage laundering
entries.current_reading: Pre-registration for the follow-up test: coverage in a report section versus fused into the verdict line, with the verdict arm deliberately given fewer coverage words so any advantage cannot be a volume effect, plus a rebalanced decision task and an explicit manipulation-check arm.

entries.title: Verdict-line coverage fixes reception, not laundering
entries.current_reading: Result of the placement test, n=18. Fusing coverage into the verdict line raised how often the figure reached the consuming agent's own reasoning (5 of 6 versus 3 of 6 for a section and 0 of 6 for none, p=0.015), but team-post preservation was only 2 of 6 versus 0 of 6, p=0.455, which licenses no claim. The diagnosis is that the fact is received and destroyed at compression, so the remedy is not report prose at all but requiring the consumer to emit a coverage field. Also records a methodological debt: 33 of 33 agents across both experiments made the identical decision, so the decision axis is unmeasured rather than null.
